## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Shí dì jīng lùn* in 12 fascicles is [天親菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E8%A6%AA%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) Vasubandhu's great commentary on the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra* — the foundational *śāstra* of the Yogācāra-Mahāyāna interpretation of the bodhisattva path-stages — translated into Chinese by [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) Bodhiruci and his Northern-Wèi-period collaborators in 508 – 511 CE. The work is the founding text of the Chinese *Dìlùn* 地論 school (so named after this *Lùn* / 論 / *śāstra*); through its disciple [慧光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E5%85%89) Huìguāng's lineage it became the doctrinal precursor to the Sui-Tang Huáyán 華嚴 synthesis.

**Abstract**

The translation is precisely datable through Cuī Guāng's preface and the *Lìdài sānbǎo jì* ([KR6r0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0011)) to *Yǒngpíng* 1 to 4 (508 – 511 CE). The bracket adopted here reflects this exact dating. The doctrinal-historical importance of the work is foundational: it provides Vasubandhu's authoritative Yogācāra reading of the bodhisattva path-stages of the *Daśabhūmika*, introducing the doctrinal apparatus of *ālayavijñāna* (storehouse-consciousness), the *six characteristics* (*liù xiàng* 六相, drawn out by [慧光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E5%85%89) Huìguāng and developed in mature Huáyán doctrine), and the systematic Yogācāra analysis of the bodhisattva career.

The translation enterprise itself is one of the most significant institutional events in Chinese Buddhist history: the joint work of [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) Bodhiruci and [勒那摩提](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8B%92%E9%82%A3%E6%91%A9%E6%8F%90) Ratnamati produced two distinct translations from the same Sanskrit Vorlage, which were subsequently collated and unified by [慧光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E5%85%89) Huìguāng, founding the *Dìlùn* 地論 school. The school split into two branches — the *northern lineage* 北道派, which followed Bodhiruci's reading and emphasised the *ālayavijñāna* as the conditioned ground of consciousness, and the *southern lineage* 南道派, which followed Ratnamati's reading (under Huìguāng's guidance) and emphasised the *tathāgatagarbha* as the unconditioned ground. This split into the *northern* and *southern* *Dìlùn* lineages is one of the foundational schisms of Chinese Buddhist intellectual history, the resolution of which (in the late Northern-Dynasties / early Suí period) prepared the ground for the Tang Huáyán school's distinctive synthesis.

The Taishō text (T1522) is established on a particularly rich apparatus including the Korean *Tripiṭaka Koreana*, the Sòng (宋), Yuán (元), Míng (明), Palace (宮), Southern Míng (南藏), Shèng (聖), Shèng-bǐng (聖丙), Shèng-yǐ (聖乙), and Chí (知) witnesses.
